title: Spend all: labs must spend all their money, 4 setups × 20 runs, $0.15 a lab (Nov 7)

design.question: For the same agents, checker and money, does a community prove more targets when value flows back (OSO) than when results are only shared, or kept private until a target is proved?
design.compare: Shared library, OSO, α 0.8, OSO, α 0.2, Traditional
design.fixed: the same 4 agents (the single agent: the first, with all the money), $0.60 in all, Lean checks every proof
design.measure: targets proved by the end of a run, of 8; money to reach 3 targets is shown beside it

answer: OSO, α 0.8 proved 5.80 (95% range 5.33 to 6.27) targets of 8 a run; Shared library 5.85 (95% range 5.58 to 6.12). Difference: -0.05 (95% range -0.59 to 0.49). OSO, α 0.2 proved 6.25 (95% range 5.80 to 6.70) targets of 8 a run; Shared library 5.85 (95% range 5.58 to 6.12). Difference: 0.40 (95% range -0.13 to 0.93).

caveats: Labs could not stop early: each worked until its money or the rounds ran out, so setups are compared at the same money spent.

Rewards differ from the current simulation model: the knowledge reward is off (the simulation pays 1 per new bit since v5): Lean has no agreed measure of a result's new knowledge yet, see docs/design.md; value flowing back is split by the money spent proving each parent, not by the work a parent saves (1/p) as in the simulation.
Table values are mean ± standard deviation over runs. Above: means with 95% ranges (Student t), and differences between setups with their 95% ranges; runs are not paired.

Money in the results is tokens at a fixed reference price per model (src/lean/prices.ts), not what the provider charged on the day, so runs on different days compare. The cost below is what was charged.
